req.title: Return DELETE request metadata
req.statement: The system shall respond to DELETE /delete with JSON including url, args, headers, form, data, files, json and origin.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that DELETE /delete returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing exactly the keys: url, args, headers, form, data, files, json, and origin. Tests are designed to: (1) verify the positive path with a plain DELETE request and assert all required keys exist with exact types/values; (2) verify query-string args are reflected; (3) verify JSON body is reflected; (4) verify that sending a wrong HTTP method (GET) to /delete returns 405, not 200; (5) verify boundary: empty body produces data='' and json=null; (6) verify that the origin field is present and non-empty. Each test uses exact-value assertions to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_delete_plain_returns_200_with_all_required_keys
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
No special headers or body required
actions: Create Flask test client from httpbin.core.app
Send DELETE request to /delete with no body and no query params
expected: JSON body contains exactly the keys: url, args, headers, form, data, files, json, origin
trace: R-HTTPBIN-010: system shall respond to DELETE /delete with JSON including url, args, headers, form, data, files, json and origin
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json as _json

def test_delete_plain_returns_200_with_all_required_keys():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.delete('/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert 'application/json' in r.content_type
    body = _json.loads(r.data)
    required_keys = {'url', 'args', 'headers', 'form', 'data', 'files', 'json', 'origin'}
    assert set(body.keys()) == required_keys
    assert body['args'] == {}
    assert body['form'] == {}
    assert body['data'] == ''
    assert body['json'] is None
    assert body['files'] == {}
    assert isinstance(body['headers'], dict)
    assert isinstance(body['url'], str)
    assert 'delete' in body['url']

test_delete_plain_returns_200_with_all_required_keys()

tests.name: test_delete_with_query_args_reflected_in_response
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
expected: url field contains the query string
trace: R-HTTPBIN-010: args field must reflect query parameters sent with DELETE
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json as _json

def test_delete_with_query_args_reflected_in_response():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.delete('/delete?foo=bar&baz=qux')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = _json.loads(r.data)
    assert body['args'] == {'foo': 'bar', 'baz': 'qux'}
    assert 'foo=bar' in body['url'] or 'baz=qux' in body['url']
    assert body['form'] == {}
    assert body['data'] == ''
    assert body['json'] is None

test_delete_with_query_args_reflected_in_response()

from httpbin.core import app
import json as _json

def test_delete_with_json_body_reflected_in_response():

tests.name: test_delete_headers_reflected_in_response
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send DELETE request to /delete with custom header X-Test-Header: sentinel-value
expected: headers field in response body contains X-Test-Header with value sentinel-value
trace: R-HTTPBIN-010: headers field must reflect incoming request headers
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json as _json

def test_delete_headers_reflected_in_response():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.delete(
        '/delete',
        headers={'X-Test-Header': 'sentinel-value'}
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = _json.loads(r.data)
    assert 'headers' in body
    assert isinstance(body['headers'], dict)
    headers_lower = {k.lower(): v for k, v in body['headers'].items()}
    assert headers_lower.get('x-test-header') == 'sentinel-value'

test_delete_headers_reflected_in_response()

actions: Send DELETE request to /delete with form-encoded body field=testval
trace: R-HTTPBIN-010: form field must reflect form-encoded body in DELETE request
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
import json as _json

def test_delete_with_form_data_reflected_in_form_field():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.delete(
        '/delete',
        data={'field': 'testval'},
        content_type='application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = _json.loads(r.data)
    assert body['form'] == {'field': 'testval'}
    assert body['json'] is None
    assert body['data'] == ''
    assert body['args'] == {}
